findings.summary: Both controller command digests are unrecomputable by any independent party, and fabricated digests compile to a schema-valid receipt. The controller_readback PASS lane is unfalsifiable.
detail: The queue item's own unresolved_operation 'materialize-controller-readback-input-with-reproducible-command-digests' states the requirement verbatim: command_sha256 'must be taken over the canonical JSON bytes of the argv array recorded in this queue item' and output_sha256 'over the captured stdout+stderr bytes, so an independent Shadow can recompute both digests'.

I computed the canonical-JSON sha256 of every argv array recorded in the queue (both items, 12 commands). Neither 1168b2a3059a38dc53c851df268c031ea9c67a87c6a9019bda074a2cd3b25da6 nor 8982ada51ceb5138b6d29eb9adf02329e0a4beddc6472cc96a4d2353bb56e6ad matches any of them.

Repository-wide grep for either digest returns exactly two files: issue-464-acceptance-input.json and the receipt compiled from it. The argv arrays are recorded nowhere. The captured stdout+stderr bytes behind output_sha256 fb184ea5... and 544738fd... are committed nowhere.
compile_codex_live_acceptance.py::_command validates only that the two values are 64 hex characters and that exit_code is integer zero. It never recomputes either digest against anything.

Falsifier F5 confirms the consequence by execution, not inference: fabricated digests produce a receipt that is byte-identical to the real one apart from the fabricated strings, and that receipt passes its schema with exit 0.

This is precisely the run item's declared forbidden promotion 'self_declared_controller_readback_to_verified_test_pass'. The run receipt nevertheless records lanes.controller_readback = PASS and verdict = PASS, and the run item's exit.required_verdict is PASS — so an unfalsifiable lane is load-bearing for a queue advance.
findings.mitigating_evidence: RB-09 re-derived the underlying fact by execution: the base tree really is red and the result tree really is green under two independent runners. The controller's claim is TRUE. The defect is in the mechanism carrying it, not in the fact.
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: Record the two controller argv arrays (and the captured output bytes, or a committed transcript digest over them) in the queue item or a committed controller-readback artifact, so command_sha256 and output_sha256 become recomputable. Then teach compile_codex_live_acceptance.py to recompute command_sha256 from the recorded argv rather than shape-checking it.

findings.summary: The shadow queue item is unsatisfiable as written: its exit requires a receipt, and producing that receipt necessarily turns the repository receipt gate red, because the schema id it names exists nowhere.
detail: The item declares receipt.schema 'agentic-tech-lead/codex-v2-live-run-shadow/v1' and exit.requires_receipt true.
No such schema file exists. Repository-wide grep for the id returns exactly one hit: line 107 of the queue that names it. references/contracts/ holds 19 schemas, none of them this one.
tests/run-all.sh's SCHEMA_BY_ID table has no entry for the id, so the gate's resolution step appends a failure and continues — red.

The gate skips any item whose receipt file is absent unless the item is COMPLETE (line 117-123). This item is BLOCKED_BY_PREDECESSOR, so while no receipt existed the whole defect was invisible behind a green suite.
The one-variable experiment in gate_impact_of_this_artifact proves the coupling: gate exit 0 with the receipt absent, exit 1 with it present, nothing else changed.

Consequence: any honest Shadow that satisfies exit.requires_receipt breaks the suite, and the only way to keep the suite green is to never produce the receipt the queue demands. That is a contradiction in the queue/gate pair, not a defect in the receipt.

The SCHEMA_MISMATCH_DECLARED escape hatch the gate offers (line 137, used by the #535 sibling receipt) cannot help here: it is evaluated only AFTER schema_file resolves, and resolution is what fails. A declared mismatch can survive this gate; an absent schema cannot.
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: Either author references/contracts/codex-v2-live-run-shadow-receipt.schema.json and register the id in SCHEMA_BY_ID, or point the item's receipt.schema at an existing contract. Both are outside this lane's write lease.

findings.summary: The live-run receipt's receipt_landing_commit names a commit that is not an ancestor of the current admitted main, so the receipt's own provenance field is stale.
detail: The receipt declares subject.receipt_landing_commit = 218a82407337335fe263b5d8e3b9dfc4c5924962.

`git merge-base --is-ancestor 218a8240 a9db0bd9` exits 1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 08a7d3c8 a9db0bd9` also exits 1. The merge-base of the declared landing commit and the current subject is 674cfe1435c4bd1c29e8f07308266fe5c6284973.

218a8240 lives on branches worktree-local-handoff-queue and origin/agent/local-handoff-queue-live, and its own tree does not contain issue-464-live-run-receipt.json at all — the receipt that names it landed afterwards, on a divergent line.

The declared STALE_SUBJECT failure state is nevertheless correctly NONE: the schema defines it as 'queue subject is not an ancestor of its landing commit', and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 08a7d3c8 218a8240` exits 0. The defect is that the receipt's landing-commit record was carried across a re-landing without being updated, not that the stated rule was broken.

Materially this is a record defect only, not an evidence defect: all nine reviewed artifacts have identical blob SHAs at 218a8240 and at a9db0bd9 (see bound_subjects.artifact_bytes_identical_across_landing_commit_and_read_subject).
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: Update subject.receipt_landing_commit to the commit that actually lands the receipt on the admitted line, as part of whatever re-lands it. Out of this lane's write lease.

findings.summary: Six of the seven failure_state values have zero producers. The failure enum is effectively unary.
detail: `grep -rn 'STALE_SUBJECT|SDK_RETURNED_WITHOUT_CONTROLLER_ACCEPTANCE|CHANGED_FILE_DRIFT|CONTROLLER_TEST_FAILURE|INCOMPATIBLE_RETRY_LINEAGE|MALFORMED_RESULT' skills/agentic-tech-lead-orchestration/scripts skills/agentic-tech-lead-orchestration/tests -l` exits 1 — no file matched.
No script and no test in the skill ever emits any non-NONE failure_state. The only value any artifact has ever carried is NONE, hand-authored.

The schema's stated purpose is that '#464 requires the run's failure states to remain expressible after the fact'. They are expressible in the schema and unreachable in production: a state that only a human can type is not a state the system can enter.
The schema does enforce the verdict/failure_state coupling (falsifier F6 goes red), so the enum is not decorative — but nothing produces its members.
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: Give at least the mechanically detectable members a producer — STALE_SUBJECT from the ancestry check the schema description already specifies, CHANGED_FILE_DRIFT and MALFORMED_RESULT from check_codex_worker_result.py's existing raise sites — so a failed run emits its own failure state instead of relying on hand authorship.

findings.summary: No gate anywhere checks the ancestry invariant that the receipt schema's own description states.
detail: codex-v2-live-run-receipt.schema.json documents the rule in prose ('A receipt whose queue subject is not an ancestor of its landing commit is the STALE_SUBJECT failure state') but encodes only the verdict/failure_state coupling in its allOf. JSON Schema cannot express git ancestry, which is fine — but nothing else expresses it either.
tests/run-all.sh mentions #464 exactly once, in a comment at line 246, and its control-plane block validates schema shapes only. It never resolves a commit.
assert_local_handoff_queue.py validates queue shape and exits 0 on the committed queue; it never compares any declared commit against the repository.
SH-02 is a live instance of this hole: the record is stale and every gate in the repository is green.
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: One `git merge-base --is-ancestor` assertion in the receipt paper gate would close it, and would have caught SH-02 mechanically.

findings.summary: The throwaway repository's RED test is only red under some runners; the naive invocation is green on the unfixed base tree.
detail: tests/test_calc.py defines `class T(unittest.TestCase)` with no `unittest.main()` entrypoint.

Measured on the pristine base tree: `python3 tests/test_calc.py` exits 0 (no-op), `python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p test_*.py` exits 5 (nothing collected). Both are green on code that raises NotImplementedError.
`python3 -m unittest tests/test_calc.py` and `python3 -m pytest -q` do discriminate: base 1, result 0.

The queue's required_capabilities include 'throwaway-run-repository-with-red-then-green-test'. Because SH-01 makes command_sha256 unrecomputable, an independent reviewer cannot determine which runner the controller used — and two of the five plausible runners would have produced a green that proves nothing.
This does not make the run's claim false: RB-09 confirms a real red-to-green under discriminating runners. It makes the recorded evidence unable to show which case occurred.
findings.remedy_not_performed_here: Give the canary test an explicit entrypoint, and record the runner argv (which SH-01's remedy already requires).

worker_result_sha256 782db01c... is the canonical-JSON digest of the committed worker result AND of the acceptance input's embedded copy; the two objects are equal.
